extracted.intended_audience: electric cooperative leaders, policymakers, regulatory staff, and stakeholders interested in federal permitting and reliability policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy recommendations for reforming federal permitting, NEPA implementation, disaster assistance, and related regulatory rules to protect electricity reliability and affordability (aimed at electric cooperatives and policymakers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit unnecessary litigation of NEPA reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Impose reasonable time limits on litigation challenging NEPA reviews; current statute of limitations of up to six years can be used to block infrastructure investment indefinitely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation from testimony: shorten the available post-approval litigation window so projects are not stalled for years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep NEPA neutral on procedures and technology
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA should not be used to dictate policy outcomes or compel agencies to favor one energy source or technology over another unless required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As reinforced by recent Supreme Court guidance, NEPA's role is to ensure an informed decision-making process, not to pick winners and losers among technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify scope of NEPA reviews: focus on direct, foreseeable impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA reviews should focus on direct, foreseeable environmental effects that are within an agency’s legal jurisdiction and expertise, rather than expansive indirect or upstream/downstream impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both legislative reforms and the Supreme Court decision (Seven County Infrastructure v. Eagle County) support narrowing NEPA analyses to effects of the project under review and deferring to agencies on scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set deadlines and page limits for NEPA environmental reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt concrete timelines and page limits for environmental reviews: two years and 150 pages for environmental impact statements (EIS); one year and 75 pages for environmental assessments (EA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These limits reflect the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 and are cited as ways to expedite permitting and cut project costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify that NEPA does not apply to every federal action
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should narrowly apply NEPA and recognize that not every government grant, funding action, or approval automatically triggers a NEPA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SPEED Act proposal specifically would remove automatic NEPA triggers for certain federal grants or funding to reduce repetitive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow categorical exclusions for low-impact activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should be able to create and adopt categorical exclusions for activities that do not have significant environmental impacts to streamline reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorical exclusions reduce unnecessary paperwork and speed up approvals for routine or low-impact projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require litigants to raise concerns during public comment before suing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties wishing to challenge a NEPA review in court should be required to have raised their concerns during the administrative public comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reform is advocated to prevent parties from withholding issues until after final agency action as a litigation strategy that delays projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose reasonable limits on post-approval challenge periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Shorten or otherwise make reasonable the long statute of limitations that currently allows challenges up to six years after final approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reducing the post-approval challenge window would help prevent indefinite project blocking and increase predictability for infrastructure investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA reviews should concentrate on impacts within agencies' legal mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should concentrate on direct, foreseeable environmental impacts that fall within their expertise and statutory authority when conducting NEPA analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is framed as ensuring agencies don't expand reviews far beyond their jurisdiction, which adds delay and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting reform: remove automatic NEPA trigger for federal funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Change permitting rules so that receiving federal grants or other funding would not automatically trigger a NEPA review for co-op improvement projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed in the SPEED Act to reduce repetitive NEPA reviews when federal funds are used for routine system improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasury 'start-of-construction' safe harbor standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain existing Treasury rules that construction is considered begun if significant physical work has started or the developer meets a 'safe harbor' test of paying/incurring at least 5% of total project cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA urges Treasury to keep these rules so co-ops can qualify for elective-pay tax credits without disruption to financing and project timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain elective-pay option for tax credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve utilities' ability to access energy tax credits through an elective-pay option rather than removing access via changes to 'beginning of construction' rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the rules could complicate financing, increase costs, or cause co-ops to abandon projects, raising rates for members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve access to FEMA public assistance for co-ops
rubrics_metrics.description: FEMA public assistance programs must be preserved because they are essential for co-ops to rebuild after disasters and ensure reliable, affordable power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While FEMA should be reformed, eliminating federal assistance responsibility would undermine recovery and increase costs/burden on states and co-ops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower FEMA per capita thresholds for public assistance eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce FEMA’s per capita threshold used to determine eligibility for public assistance so that cooperatives—who build more infrastructure per consumer—can qualify more easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA argues current thresholds disadvantage rural co-ops and slow disaster recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed FEMA reimbursements and reimburse interest on loans
rubrics_metrics.description: FEMA should reduce delays in disbursing public assistance funds and reimburse interest on loans that co-ops incur while waiting for FEMA payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current reimbursement timeline is often measured in years; reform would enable quicker recovery and reduce financial strain on co-ops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect nonprofits from unreasonable clawbacks and expand direct access to resiliency funds
rubrics_metrics.description: FEMA should extend protections to co-ops and other private nonprofits against unreasonable clawbacks of public assistance and provide eligible nonprofits direct access to FEMA resiliency funding programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct access to resiliency programs would help co-ops strengthen systems and reduce outages during disasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA procedural reforms should focus agencies on foreseeable impacts within expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures should modernize environmental permitting by concentrating on direct, foreseeable impacts within agencies' legal expertise and mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates the goal of procedural reforms to reduce delays, unpredictability, and unnecessary expansions of NEPA scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt predictable, expedited agency NEPA procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should implement simplified, streamlined, and predictable NEPA procedures (including time limits, page limits and categorical exclusions) to expedite permitting for energy and broadband projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA cites multi-agency July 1 procedural updates as delivering reforms they've requested for years to allow quicker project review and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational planning: review plans and operate conservatively to ensure resource availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmission owners and grid authorities should review their operating plans and operate conservatively to ensure adequate resource availability in light of rising demand and changing resource mix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC urged conservative operations to address potential near-term shortfalls and ensure reliability during extreme weather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for inverter-based resource (IBR) trips and model vulnerabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Grid operators should be prepared for the potential of inverter-based resources (solar PV and batteries) to unexpectedly trip during disturbances and plan accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC highlighted the need to consider IBR behavior during grid disturbances as a reliability risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve modeling of large, fast-deploying loads (data centers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Better models of data center and large speculative loads are needed to improve planning, worst-case scenario identification, and preparations for integrating large step-changes in load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC and DOE reports note data centers are being built faster than grid upgrades, requiring improved modeling tools for planning and mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory revisions should be workable and cost-effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory actions (e.g., EPA's coal ash rule revisions) should be developed to be workable, cost-effective, and supported by risk analyses to avoid massive costs to utilities and ratepayers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA urged the EPA to reconsider rules that adopt one-size-fits-all approaches and to delay compliance deadlines while workable revisions are developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filing of comments in rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisories about comment deadlines (e.g., comments due Aug. 7 for greenhouse gas proposal and Aug. 11 for mercury and air rule repeal) imply the procedural requirement to submit timely, substantive comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting published deadlines is necessary to participate effectively in notice-and-comment rulemakings; the piece lists specific due dates for these proposals.
